about: The sheet for the Main Street Station cutaway: tools/cutaway/sheet.py. Callouts are anchored to drawn parts (history ids, in the isometric view and the flat section); a badge's style is the anchored part's confidence unless `confidence` says otherwise. Callout text is a working draft, written with Claude, for the artist to edit.
title: Main Street Station, 1952
subtitle: Cut down the middle, from Main Street up to the trains
sectionCaption: The same cut, seen flat: Main Street on the left, the trains on the right

callouts.title: Main Street
callouts.text: East Main Street, in Shockoe Valley.

callouts.title: The loggia
callouts.text: Five segmental arches of rough-hewn stone; the first from the west opens on the main stair.

callouts.title: The main stair
callouts.text: Straight up to the waiting room without turning, with a landing halfway, between tiled walls.

callouts.title: The waiting room
callouts.text: A coffered ceiling and a screen of columns and glazed arches toward the stair. Its east half, where the ticket booths stood, is lifted away.

callouts.title: The concourse
callouts.text: An ell behind the head house, open to the shed. Its roof is lifted away.

callouts.title: The gates
callouts.text: A wrought-iron screen with numbered gates.

callouts.title: Platforms and tracks
callouts.text: Six stub tracks and five platforms, level with the waiting room, and a through track under each eave.

callouts.title: The trains
callouts.text: Seaboard Air Line trains used the west side, Chesapeake and Ohio trains the east.

callouts.title: A diesel
callouts.text: A streamlined cab unit of about 1950, in plain form: no source shows which engine stood here.

callouts.title: The train shed
callouts.text: Riveted steel by Wilson Brothers, 1900, 123 by 517 ft: trusses 18 ft apart, a monitor on the ridge.

callouts.title: On trestles
callouts.text: Steel trestles carry the tracks, and bridges carry them over Main Street.

callouts.title: Mail and baggage
callouts.text: Baggage rooms and a public hall on the ground floor; the mail room under the concourse, docks on the west.

callouts.title: Offices
callouts.text: Three floors of offices on an east-west corridor, two of them in the roof, lit by dormers.

callouts.title: The clock tower
callouts.text: Six stories at the southwest corner; its finial stands 110 ft above the ground.

key: drawn from a plan, a section or a survey map
marksNote: The same marks stand by each place the trains went.
sources: Sources: HAER VA-4, the train shed (drawings, 1970; photographs, 1971) and HABS VA-848, the station (data pages, 1969; photographs), Library of Congress; National Register (1970) and Landmark (1976) nominations; Detroit Publishing photographs, about 1905; Official Guide, December 1952; SAH Archipedia; OpenStreetMap; USGS 3DEP.
notes: No plan of the head house is known: its rooms follow the HABS description, its heights and stonework are scaled from photographs. Virginia law segregated the waiting rooms in 1952; no source found says where.
